classification.difficultyReason: Interpret matching ticks, build and equate the two perimeter expressions, then use the solved side lengths to calculate the rectangle’s area.

inlines.text: The perimeter of the triangle is the same as the perimeter of the rectangle.
Work out the area of the rectangle.

spec.description: Upright isosceles triangle with one matching tick on each sloping side, right sloping-side label 3x + 1, and a double-ended dimension arrow labelled 2x below the horizontal base.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels and equality marks are permanent student-visible givens; no answers are drawn.

spec.description: Horizontal rectangle with a double-ended horizontal dimension arrow labelled x + 7 above its top edge and a double-ended vertical dimension arrow labelled x outside its right edge.
spec.answerVisibility: Both dimension labels are permanent student-visible givens; no answers are drawn.

answer.short: $30$ square units. Equal perimeters give $8x+2=4x+14$, so $x=3$.
answer.worked:
The matching ticks show that both sloping sides have length $3x+1$.

$$\begin{align*}P_{\text{triangle}}&=2x+(3x+1)+(3x+1)=8x+2\\P_{\text{rectangle}}&=2(x+7)+2x=4x+14\end{align*}$$

Equate the perimeters and subtract $4x$ from both sides:

$$\begin{align*}8x+2&=4x+14\\4x+2&=14\\4x&=12\\x&=3\end{align*}$$

The rectangle has side lengths $3$ and $3+7=10$.

$$A=3(3+7)=30$$

Its area is $30$ square units. Check: both perimeters are $26$ units.
